intro: You clicked "I agree" on Hollowmere Cloud without reading a word, and now the paperwork has come to collect. The office door has sealed itself, and the ghosts of the fine print won't let you leave until you prove you know what you signed.
verdict: Paid plans renew automatically, and fees you've already paid are non-refundable.
Hollowmere gets a broad licence to use your files, including to promote its services, and can scan them for faces and objects.
Your usage information is shared with advertising partners.
Disputes go to individual arbitration, and you give up class actions unless you opt out within 30 days.
If anything goes wrong, Hollowmere's liability can be as little as £50.

puzzles.title: The watching portrait
puzzles.riddle: The painted eyes follow you around the room. "I see everything you do," it whispers, "and I tell my friends."
puzzles.question: Who does Hollowmere share your usage information with?
puzzles.quote: We share usage information with our advertising partners so they can show you more relevant offers.
puzzles.plain_english: How you use the app is passed to advertisers to target you with offers. Your actual files aren't sold.
hints: The portrait cares about your data. Look in section 4.
Section 4.2 names exactly who your usage information goes to.

puzzles.title: The grandfather clock
puzzles.riddle: The pendulum stops. "Forget me long enough," the clock tolls, "and everything you stored is mine."
puzzles.question: After how many months without signing in can a free account be treated as abandoned?
puzzles.quote: If you do not sign in to a free account for 13 consecutive months, we may treat the account as abandoned.
puzzles.plain_english: If you ignore a free account for a little over a year, Hollowmere can warn you once and then delete everything in it 30 days later.
hints: Clocks count time away. Find the section about inactive accounts.
Section 5.1 gives a number of consecutive months.

puzzles.title: The bookshelf of closed cases
puzzles.riddle: One spine is cold to the touch. "No judge, no jury, no crowd of fellow victims," it murmurs. "Just you, alone, before me."
puzzles.question: Disputes that aren't resolved informally are settled by binding individual what?
puzzles.quote: Any dispute that is not resolved informally will be settled by binding individual arbitration, and you waive any right to take part in a class action or representative proceeding.
puzzles.plain_english: You can't take Hollowmere to court or join a class action. Disputes go to a private arbitrator, one person at a time, unless you opt out within 30 days.
hints: The bookshelf is full of legal disputes. Look in section 8.
Section 8.2 says how unresolved disputes are settled.

puzzles.title: The solicitor's desk
puzzles.riddle: Your holiday photos are pinned to the desk, and something has drawn a circle around every face.
puzzles.question: What can Hollowmere's automated systems recognise in your content?
puzzles.quote: You agree that we may use automated systems to analyse Your Content, including to recognise faces and objects, in order to build features such as smart albums.
puzzles.plain_english: Hollowmere scans what you upload, including running face recognition on your photos, to build features.
hints: The desk holds your uploads. Section 3 is about Your Content.
Section 3.3 says what the automated systems recognise.

puzzles.title: The iron safe
puzzles.riddle: The safe rattles with loose change. "Lose everything," it sneers, "and this is all you'll get back, at the very least."
puzzles.question: What is the minimum amount, in pounds, that Hollowmere's total liability is capped at?
puzzles.quote: To the maximum extent permitted by law, our total liability to you for any claim relating to the service is limited to the greater of the fees you paid us in the 12 months before the claim, or £50.
puzzles.plain_english: If Hollowmere loses your files, the most you can claim is what you paid in the last year, or £50 if that's more.
hints: The safe is about money owed to you. Look for liability in section 7.
Section 7.2 ends with a sum in pounds.
